name: Whitening gel trays

lead: Whitening gel trays are soft plastic trays loaded with a carbamide or hydrogen peroxide gel and worn over the teeth for minutes to hours at a time. They come as custom-fitted trays made by a dentist from impressions or scans, or as boil-and-bite and prefilled over-the-counter versions.
Because the tray holds gel against every tooth surface, coverage is more even than with strips, and dentist-supervised take-home bleaching is regarded as a standard cosmetic dental option.

paras: Carbamide peroxide breaks down into hydrogen peroxide and urea, and the released peroxide oxidizes pigment molecules inside enamel and dentin. A well-fitted tray keeps gel in constant contact with the teeth and away from the gums, allowing longer, lower-concentration exposure.

Tooth sensitivity and gum irritation are the common effects and are typically temporary; poorly fitting trays let gel leak onto the gums. A meta-analysis found tray carbamide peroxide and hydrogen peroxide systems comparable overall, and supervised trays give slightly larger measured color change than strips, though the difference may not be visible. Ill-fitting low-cost trays lose much of the coverage advantage, and a dental check beforehand is commonly recommended.
